processing: A cultivar rather than a finished tea, so processing depends on the maker. Little is documented for it specifically; the usual Chinese green tea sequence is fixing, shaping and drying.
harvest_season: Not well documented. The name's zao (早, early) points to early budding, and Chinese green teas are generally most prized from the first spring pickings.
appearance_dry: Varies with the style it is made into; as with most Chinese spring greens, expect green, tender buds and young leaves.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Chinese spring greens: pale yellow-green and clear.
appearance_wet: Typical of Chinese spring greens: soft green buds and young leaves.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting description exists for this cultivar on its own; a cup made from it should be judged as a Chinese spring green, usually fresh and gently vegetal.

brewing.notes: General advice for a delicate Chinese green: cooler water and an open glass or gaiwan. Adjust to the actual tea in hand.

vintage_note: Rarely sold under the cultivar name alone. As is usual for Chinese green teas, leaf from any cultivar is sold as the current year's spring harvest and is best drunk within a year.
description:
Anmingzao is a named cultivar of the tea plant, not a tea style. If you see the name, it tells you which bush the leaf came from, while the style of the finished tea is a separate question.

Very little is documented about how it behaves in the cup. The zao in its name means early, a common way of naming early-budding cultivars, but specific figures on budding date, yield or chemistry are not documented in general references.

Brew it the way you would brew the green tea it has been made into. For a typical Chinese spring green that means water around 80 C and a light hand with the leaf.

When buying, ask for the place and picking date as well as the cultivar. Those two facts tell you more about what will be in the cup than the cultivar name alone.
history: Little is documented about this cultivar in general reference material. Its breeder, year of release and parentage are not on the general record.
sources_note: Chinese name taken from the master row; no page describing the cultivar was read.
